Index: package.json
===================================================================
--- package.json	
+++ package.json	
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+{
+  "name": "expand-range",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "description": "Expand ranges like \"1-10\" or \"a-z\" into an array of values",
+  "type": "module",
+  "main": "src/expand-range.js",
+  "exports": "./src/expand-range.js",
+  "bin": {
+    "expand-range": "bin/expand-range.js"
+  },
+  "scripts": {
+    "test": "node --test"
+  },
+  "engines": {
+    "node": ">=18"
+  },
+  "license": "MIT"
+}

parts.text:
There's one issue with the CLI usage error: when no args, process.exit(1) fine. Also package.json bin points to bin/expand-range.js which imports from ../src relative to bin — good.

Now run tests and CLI. Also the "1-a" case: regex `^(-?\d+|[A-Za-z])-(-?\d+|[A-Za-z])$` — for '1-a', start '1' numeric, end 'a' letter -> both tests won't be true, so throws "both" error. Good.

But wait, "1-a" regex: first group -?\d+ matches '1', '-' then [A-Za-z] matches 'a'. Yes.

Run tests.

parts.text:
Project set up with zero dependencies (uses Node's built-in test runner):

- `package.json` — ESM package, `bin`, `npm test` script
- `src/expand-range.js` — `expandRange('1-10')` → `[1..10]`, `'a-z'` → `['a'..'z']`; supports descending ranges, negative numbers, whitespace
- `bin/expand-range.js` — CLI printing JSON
- `test/expand-range.test.js` — 8 tests, all passing

Usage: `npm test`, or `node bin/expand-range.js "a-z"`.
